content.text: Zion Williamson’s and-one drive gave New Orleans a lead in the final minute. Yves Missi’s defense against Anthony Edwards preserved it.After three straight narrow defeats to begin a week-long road trip, New Orleans roared back from an 18-point second-half deficit at Minnesota on Friday to stun the Timberwolves in dramatic fashion. With Minnesota leading 115-114, Williamson converted a physical, three-point play with 35 seconds remaining. On the next possession, Missi was switched onto Timberwolves top threat Edwards, forcing the All-Star into a difficult mid-range shot that came up well short. Saddiq Bey then sank two free throws with 10 seconds to go, making it a two-possession margin.“To be able to rally in the (second half) and come up with a win is big for us,” Williamson said, referring to 33-24 and 30-21 advantages on the scoreboard for New Orleans in the third and fourth quarters, respectively. The Pelicans experienced frustrating previous games at Philadelphia, Charlotte and Milwaukee, all decided down the stretch or in overtime, unable to pull off a victory despite holding late leads or having opportunities in clutch time.Video Player is loading.Current Time 0:00Duration 1:57Remaining Time 1:57Zion Williamson Highlights vs. Minnesota Timberwolves 2/6/26BY THE NUMBERS18: Most three-pointers over a two-game span by any New Orleans player in franchise history, a mark Trey Murphy set in the third quarter with his fifth triple of that period. He followed up his dozen makes Wednesday at Milwaukee with a total of six in Minnesota (26 points on 9/15 shooting). “Trey is a special player,” Williamson said. “He continues to get better, day by day. Those threes (in the third quarter) he hit were big-time for us. We went from being down 14, 15 (points) to right back in the game.”30: Bey points, with 14 of those coming in the fourth period, capping by him going 4/4 on free throws in the final 70 seconds. Williamson added seven points in that stanza among his total of 29, while reserve Bryce McGowens converted two critical buckets among his six final-quarter points.4/4: Derik Queen three-point shooting, sinking one trey in every quarter. The rookie has been an erratic shooter from the perimeter in 2025-26 as he tries to develop that aspect of his arsenal, but his accuracy Friday provided a big boost. The Pelicans also have three straight home tilts after the All-Star break, meaning their next road contest isn’t until Feb. 26 at Utah.NEXT VS. TIMBERWOLVESNew Orleans and Minnesota played a fairly memorable Game 82 in Minneapolis to conclude the 2022-23 regular season, with a Timberwolves victory dropping the Pelicans to a No. 9 seed (they lost the 9-10 play-in game to Oklahoma City three days later). Two-plus months from now, Target Center will again be the venue for the finale of a regular season for these two clubs.
